turns.question: Where is middleware composition implemented?
turns.text:
I'll explore the Hono repository structure to locate middleware composition logic.There's a dedicated `src/compose.ts` file. Let me read it along with `hono-base.ts` (where the router/handler pipeline is built) to see how composition connects into the request lifecycle.I have enough to give a complete answer.

## Middleware composition in honojs/hono

**Core implementation: `src/compose.ts`, function `compose`**

This is the heart of Hono's middleware/handler pipeline, explicitly modeled on `koa-compose`:

```ts
export const compose = <E extends Env = Env>(
  middleware: [[Function, unknown], unknown][] | [[Function]][],
  onError?: ErrorHandler<E>,
  onNotFound?: NotFoundHandler<E>
): ((context: Context, next?: Next) => Promise<Context>)
```

It returns a function that runs a recursive `dispatch(i)`: each middleware in the array is invoked with `(context, () => dispatch(i + 1))`, so calling `next()` inside a middleware advances to the next one in the chain (classic onion-model composition). It guards against `next()` being called twice (`if (i <= index) throw new Error('next() called multiple times')`), catches thrown errors and routes them to `onError`, and falls back to `onNotFound` when no handler matched. Evidence: full source read at `src/compose.ts`.

**Where `compose` is invoked: `src/hono-base.ts`**

- `#dispatch()` (the method that backs `app.fetch`) matches routes via `this.router.match(method, path)`, producing `matchResult[0]` — an array of `[handler, routeInfo]` pairs (all middleware + the final route handler registered for that path/method). 
  - As an optimization, if only one handler matched (`matchResult[0].length === 1`), it's invoked directly without composing (`src/hono-base.ts:429-448`).
  - Otherwise: `const composed = compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)` then `await composed(c)` (`src/hono-base.ts:450-454`).
- `.route()` (sub-app mounting) also uses `compose([], app.errorHandler)(c, () => r.handler(c, next))` to wrap a mounted sub-app's error handler around its routes (`src/hono-base.ts:222-226`).

**How middleware arrays are built: `router.add`**

`app.use(path, ...middlewares)` and `app.get/post/etc` (in `hono-base.ts`, via `#addRoute`) each call `this.router.add(method, path, [handler, routeInfo])`. The router (e.g. `RegExpRouter`, `TrieRouter`, `SmartRouter` in `src/router/*`) is responsible for collecting, for a given incoming path, the ordered list of all matching `[handler, ...]` entries — that ordered list is exactly the `middleware` array passed into `compose`. I did not verify the internal matching/ordering logic of each router implementation (`src/router/reg-exp-router`, `src/router/trie-router`, etc.) — only confirmed they're the source of `matchResult[0]`.

**Higher-level composition helpers: `src/middleware/combine/index.ts`**

Built on top of `compose` for conditional middleware combination:
- `some(...)` — runs middleware until one succeeds.
- `every(...)` — runs all, short-circuits on failure; implemented by calling `compose(middleware.map(...))(c, next)` directly, reusing the same core primitive.
- `except(condition, ...middleware)` — skips middleware when a path/condition matches, built from `some` + `every`.

### Summary of key files/symbols
| File | Symbol | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `src/compose.ts` | `compose()` | Core onion-model middleware composer (dispatch/next chain) |
| `src/hono-base.ts` | `#dispatch()`, `#addRoute()`, `.route()` | Builds matched handler arrays and invokes `compose` |
| `src/router.ts` + `src/router/*` | `Router.add`, `Router.match` | Supplies the ordered handler list per request (not deeply verified) |
| `src/middleware/combine/index.ts` | `some`, `every`, `except` | Higher-level conditional composition, reusing `compose` |

Not verified: internal ordering guarantees of each concrete router (`RegExpRouter`/`TrieRouter`/`SmartRouter`/`LinearRouter`/`PatternRouter`) for how they assemble the middleware chain — I only confirmed they feed `compose` via `matchResult[0]`.
